label: Abstract: descriptive universal collapse
old:
Categorical proof theory expresses identifications of proofs as
equations between arrows. We prove that the zero-identity Boolean
category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set
of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining an equation between
distinct arrows with the same source and target, and closing under
the arrow operations and uniform formula substitution, identifies
all parallel arrows.
new:
Categorical proof theory expresses identifications of proofs as
equations between arrows. We study the zero-identity Boolean
category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty
set of propositional variables. We prove that adjoining any equation
between parallel arrows that does not follow from the defining
equations, and closing under the arrow operations and uniform
formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder.
All arrows with the same source and target then become equal.

label: Introduction: result before terminology
old:
Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c conjecture that their freely generated
zero-identity Boolean category is not maximal
\cite[\S14.2, p.~322]{DP}. We prove that it is maximal. Any equation
between parallel arrows that does not already hold, when closed under
the arrow operations and uniform formula substitution, identifies
every pair of parallel arrows.
new:
We consider the freely generated zero-identity Boolean category of
Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c over a nonempty set of propositional variables.
We prove that adding any equation between parallel arrows that does
not follow from its defining equations, and closing under the arrow
operations and uniform formula substitution, collapses the category
to a preorder. All arrows with the same source and target then
become equal. This property is called maximality. Do\v{s}en and
Petri\'c conjecture that the category is not maximal
\cite[\S14.2, p.~322]{DP}.

label: Theorem 2.1: preorder conclusion
old:
Let $P$ be a nonempty set of propositional variables. The freely
generated zero-identity Boolean category $\B(P)$ of Do\v{s}en and
Petri\'c is maximal. Equivalently, every substitution congruence on
$\B(P)$ that identifies two distinct parallel arrows identifies all
parallel arrows.
new:
Let $P$ be a nonempty set of propositional variables, and let
$\B(P)$ be the freely generated zero-identity Boolean category of
Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c. For every substitution congruence $\theta$
on $\B(P)$ that identifies two distinct parallel arrows, the
quotient $\B(P)/\theta$ is a preorder.

label: Section 2: explain maximality after stating the result
new:
\emph{Maximality} means that this collapse occurs for every added
equation between parallel arrow terms that does not follow from the
defining equations, with closure under the arrow operations and
uniform substitution. Equivalently, the only substitution
congruences are equality and the total congruence.
Sections~\ref{sec:isolation} and~\ref{sec:collapse} give the proof.
